explanation: The war’s article begins the Japanese expansion it grew out of at Shandong, which Japan took from Germany’s sphere after 1918. The article reads: "Following World War I, Japan acquired the German Empire's sphere of influence in Shandong province, leading to nationwide anti-Japanese protests and mass demonstrations in China."

retraction.reason: A14(4): one of the eleven A13 edges whose quote opens "Following", "After" or "In the aftermath", re-read under the fire's own refusal class — chronology with no claim in it. A13 asks for an edge where the article states that one event caused, enabled, preceded or reacted to the other, and here the sentence says Japan acquired the German sphere in Shandong following the war, "leading to nationwide anti-Japanese protests" — the May Fourth movement of 1919, not the war of 1937. The 24 September review read it in full and called it chronology. The quote stays in this record; what is withdrawn is the claim that the article made the link.
